newsitem.title: MEXICO: Family says Mexico's most notorious drug lord dead.
newsitem.headline: Family says Mexico's most notorious drug lord dead.

text.p: Mexico's most wanted drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, has died of a heart attack, his mother said on Saturday. Officials were unable to confirm the report.
Aurora Fuentes de Carrillo told reporters gathered at her luxury ranch in the village of Guamuchilito in northwestern Sinaloa state that rumours of her son's death were true.
The drug baron's mother told reporters her son died of a heart attack during surgery in Mexico City, radio network Radio Red said. The report did not say when Carrillo died.
Mexico's Attorney General's Office said in a statement it could not confirm Carrillo's death until it had examined the corpse.
"Until now, although people close to Mr. Carrillo Fuentes have supposedly confirmed the news, the Attorney General's office is not able to confirm the reports," the statement said.
"This confirmation must wait until we have had access to the corpse and there has been a medical examination," it added.
Spokeswomen at the Attorney-General's office were unable to say whether investigators had already located a possible Carrillo body or were still searching for the corpse.

Police said Carrillo, believed to be 42, has shipped billions of dollars of cocaine a year through Mexico to the United States. He heads the so-called Juarez cartel, based in the northern border city of Ciudad Juarez, next to El Paso, Texas.

Carrillo has already had several narrow escapes. He was arrested in 1989 but later released. A few years later he made a dramatic escape when rival mobsters tried to gun him down as he dined with his family in a Mexico City restaurant.
On that occasion, Carrillo clambered to safety through a toilet window as his bodyguards fired back at the assailants.

Since he went underground, few pictures of Carrillo exist. The most recent were images from a video shot at his sister's wedding in January, showing the portly trafficker attending the ceremony dressed in a jacket and tie and hugging his wife.

Efforts by Mexican authorities to catch the elusive capo have proven fruitless for more than eight years, exposing the government to criticism from U.S. lawmakers that it was not doing enough to fight drugs.
The last known operation against Carrillo was at his sister's wedding, when soldiers and police stormed the reception in the Guamuchilito ranch but failed to find their prey.

An army major was later arrested for having allegedly tipped off the drug lord and allowing him to escape. Embarrassed Mexican officials initially claimed Carrillo had not been at the wedding but the video of his presence contradicted them.

Carrillo's wealth allowed him to bribe scores of Mexican officials. Mexico's former anti-drugs chief, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, was jailed in February on charges he had taken bribes from Carrillo.
